items_missed: Never got the customer's actual name — asked for the 'name used online' and got 'Marlene' (an online profile name), never learned or used 'Robert' during the call
No 'how are you today?' and no agenda statement/'sound good?' framing at the start of the call
Didn't ask about additional rooms (garage/storage unit/balcony), storage stops, or additional stops
Didn't explain walk distance from truck to door or use a size/equivalents reference (e.g. school bus comparison) to help the customer visualize the move
No Save Your Ass prep speech at all — no consolidation tips (toys, drawers, garden tools) and no 'take a carload' advice
Never attempted to book/schedule the move on the call and never mentioned 'no deposit required'
Didn't ask the customer to reply with corrections to the confirmation email, didn't ask 'any other questions before I let you go?', and didn't give branch hours/how to reach the office
Insurance explanation covered the $2,000 No Worries Damage Coverage but omitted the 60¢/lb baseline valuation option
No rapport-building humor or personal warmth beyond the transactional pricing walkthrough
top_strength: Nailed the full pricing/differentiators section cleanly and accurately — hourly rate with Saturday tier, what's included, trip fee, No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the no-hidden-fees pitch all landed, paired with a well-reasoned itemized time/price estimate that adjusted down once she learned the dining table was already disassembled and the drive was only 8 miles.
coaching_note: Get and use the caller's actual name early instead of relying on the online profile name (she called him 'Marlene' when speaking with Robert), and close the loop before hanging up — no Save Your Ass prep speech, no explicit booking attempt, and no 'no deposit required' line, even though the customer was clearly deciding then and there.
phone_presence_notes: Professional, patient, and thorough walking a confused caller through pricing, but transactional throughout — no affirmations, no name use, and rapport never went beyond the task at hand.
